name: FRAPPE_GET
label: Get Field Value
description:
Fetch any single field from any Frappe document.
=FRAPPE_GET(doctype, name, fieldname)

name: FRAPPE_SUM
label: Sum Field Across Records
description:
Sum any numeric field across a DocType, with up to 4 filter pairs.
=FRAPPE_SUM(doctype, fieldname [, fk1, fv1, ...])

name: FRAPPE_COUNT
label: Count Records
description:
Count records in any DocType, with up to 3 filter pairs.
=FRAPPE_COUNT(doctype [, fk1, fv1, fk2, fv2, fk3, fv3])

name: FRAPPE_AVG
label: Average Field Value
description:
Average any numeric field across a DocType, with up to 3 filter pairs.
=FRAPPE_AVG(doctype, fieldname [, fk1, fv1, fk2, fv2, fk3, fv3])

name: GL_BALANCE
label: General Ledger Balance
description:
Fetch live GL balance for any account.
=GL_BALANCE(account, company [, from_date, to_date, cost_center, finance_book])

name: STOCK_QTY
label: Stock Quantity
description:
Live stock quantity from Bin.
=STOCK_QTY(item_code, warehouse [, as_of_date])

name: ITEM_PRICE
label: Item Price
description:
Fetch item price from a Price List.
=ITEM_PRICE(item_code, price_list [, qty, customer, uom])

name: SMART_LOOKUP
label: Smart Cross-DocType Lookup
description:
Schema-aware cross-doctype lookup — no manual range needed.
=SMART_LOOKUP(value, target_doctype, return_field [, source_doctype])

name: PERIOD_START
label: Period Start Date
description:
Returns the start date of the active period set in the toolbar.
=PERIOD_START()

name: PERIOD_END
label: Period End Date
description:
Returns the end date of the active period set in the toolbar.
=PERIOD_END()

name: FRAPPE_CHILD_GET
label: Child Table Row Value
description:
Fetch one field from a specific row (1-based) of a child table.
=FRAPPE_CHILD_GET(parent_doctype, parent_name, child_field, row_index, fieldname)
Example: =FRAPPE_CHILD_GET("Sales Invoice", "SINV-0001", "items", 1, "amount")

name: FRAPPE_MAX
label: Max Field Value
description:
Return the maximum value of any field across a DocType, with up to 3 filter pairs. Works for dates, numbers, and strings.
=FRAPPE_MAX(doctype, fieldname [, fk1, fv1, fk2, fv2, fk3, fv3])
Example: =FRAPPE_MAX("Sales Order", "transaction_date", "customer", A2)

name: FRAPPE_MIN
label: Min Field Value
description:
Return the minimum value of any field across a DocType, with up to 3 filter pairs. Works for dates, numbers, and strings.
=FRAPPE_MIN(doctype, fieldname [, fk1, fv1, fk2, fv2, fk3, fv3])
Example: =FRAPPE_MIN("Sales Order", "transaction_date", "customer", A2)
